output:
This relaxation looks clean. The structure converged with negligible displacement and the cubic Fm-3m symmetry was preserved end-to-end.

The largest atomic displacement was 0.04 Å and the cell volume changed by only 0.2%. No bonds were broken or formed and every atom kept its original 6-fold coordination. There is nothing here that suggests an optimization problem.

This looks like a textbook ionic relaxation around an already-good starting structure. No manual review needed unless you have an external reason to doubt the input.

This relaxation looks broken and needs manual review before being trusted.

Atom 4 (Ti) traveled 3.8 Å, the cell volume collapsed by 31%, and the original I4_1/amd symmetry dropped all the way to P1. Several Ti–O bonds broke and coordination numbers shifted across the cell. These signatures together are not consistent with a normal relaxation around a metastable basin.

The pattern is consistent with either a bad initial guess (atoms placed too close, or a swapped lattice vector) or with the optimizer crossing a barrier into a much denser polymorph. I would re-check the input POSCAR, the pseudopotentials, and the relaxation step size before drawing any physical conclusion from this final structure.
